title: Government Restricts Manufacture, Sale and Distribution of Fixed Dose Combinations Containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride for Use in Children Below Four Years
body_text:
In a significant step to safeguard the health and safety of young children, the Government has imposed restrictions on the manufacture, sale and distribution of all Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride, mandating a clear warning that these medicines shall not be used in children below four years of age.
Earlier, vide notification dated 15 April 2025 [S.O. 1717(E)], the Government had restricted certain FDCs containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride, subject to the same age-specific warning. The latest notification extends this requirement to all formulations containing these two ingredients.
The decision has been taken following the recommendations of an Expert Committee and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB). The Government noted that the use of such combinations may pose risks to children below four years of age and that safer alternatives are available.
Manufacturers have been directed to clearly display the warning, “Fixed Dose Combination shall not be used in children below four years of age,” on the label, package insert and promotional literature associated with these formulations.
The notification has been issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, in the interest of public health and is effective from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
The Official Gazette can be accessed through this: https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2026/275640.pdf

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

enrichment.summary: The Union Health Ministry has extended restrictions to all Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride, mandating a label warning that they must not be used in children below four years. This builds on an earlier notification of 15 April 2025 that restricted only certain such FDCs. The move follows recommendations of an Expert Committee and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), and has been issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, citing risks to young children and availability of safer alternatives.
enrichment.context:
Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) combine two or more active pharmaceutical ingredients in a single dosage form; while convenient, irrational or unsafe FDCs have long been a regulatory concern in India, with periodic bans issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 based on DTAB recommendations. Chlorpheniramine Maleate (an antihistamine) and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride (a decongestant) are commonly used in cough-and-cold formulations, and paediatric use of such combinations has drawn global scrutiny due to reports of adverse effects, including respiratory depression and cardiovascular risks in very young children, prompting regulators in several countries to caution against decongestant-antihistamine use in children under four to six years.

This notification is a further tightening of an earlier partial restriction (April 2025), reflecting the pattern of graded regulatory action in India's drug safety framework, where Expert Committees and DTAB periodically review evidence before recommending outright bans, age restrictions, or labelling changes. Such actions are part of a broader effort to rationalise irrational FDCs and prevent misuse in vulnerable populations, especially children, echoing similar past crackdowns like the 2016 ban on hundreds of FDCs.

prelims_questions.question: The Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), mentioned in context of drug regulation in India, functions under which legislation?
prelims_questions.explanation: DTAB is the highest statutory technical body advising the Central and State Governments on technical matters under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and its recommendations underpin actions like restricting FDCs under Section 26A of the same Act.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'Fixed Dose Combination' (FDC) in pharmaceutical regulation?
options: A drug approved only for veterinary use
A single dosage form containing two or more active pharmaceutical ingredients
A drug manufactured exclusively by government pharmaceutical units
A vaccine combination for immunisation schedules only
prelims_questions.explanation: FDCs combine two or more active pharmaceutical ingredients in one dosage form; their rational use and safety, especially in children, is a recurring regulatory concern in India.

mains_questions.question: Examine the regulatory mechanisms available under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 to address the sale of irrational or unsafe fixed dose combinations in India. Discuss the challenges in ensuring drug safety for vulnerable groups such as children.

Discuss the role of institutions like the Drugs Technical Advisory Board in India's pharmaceutical regulatory framework and evaluate the effectiveness of periodic restrictions on fixed dose combinations in safeguarding public health.

prelims.point: Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) is the statutory body under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 that recommends technical/regulatory action on drugs including FDC restrictions.
prelims.syllabus: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies
prelims.why_important: DTAB's role as the technical advisory body behind such notifications is a recurring fact in drug-regulation questions.

prelims.point: The restriction covers Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) of Chlorpheniramine Maleate (antihistamine) and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride (decongestant), banned for use in children below four years.
prelims.why_important: Aspirants should know the specific age threshold and drug combination used as a factual anchor for this notification.

prelims.point: Definition: Fixed Dose Combination (FDC) refers to a single dosage form containing two or more active pharmaceutical ingredients in fixed ratios.
prelims.why_important: UPSC could test the definition of FDC and distinguish it from other drug formulation types.

prelims.point: This notification (2026) extends and builds upon an earlier partial restriction notified on 15 April 2025 [S.O. 1717(E)] covering only certain FDCs of the same ingredients.
prelims.why_important: Shows the graded/staged nature of regulatory tightening, useful for sequencing-based prelims questions.

mains.point: The action reflects India's ongoing struggle to rationalise irrational FDCs, given past instances like the 2016 ban on hundreds of combinations, raising questions about the adequacy and speed of pharmacovigilance mechanisms.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on challenges in India's drug regulatory framework or the effectiveness of post-market surveillance.

mains.point: The graded approach — first restricting select FDCs then extending to all — highlights the evidence-based, iterative nature of expert-committee-driven regulation, but also exposes delays in protecting vulnerable populations like children.
mains.theme: Regulatory governance and child health protection
mains.analytical_use: Could support an answer on balancing scientific caution with timely public health intervention in drug regulation.
